title: Explicit prime counting: numerically explicit bounds for ψ, θ, π, the n-th prime, sums over primes, primes in progressions and short intervals
summary: Explicit transfer identities between ψ, θ, π and Li; the computational hypotheses as named propositions, including the real-zero gap for real Dirichlet L-functions; bounds under RH (Lee–Nosal, Schoenfeld) and RH to a height (Büthe, Johnston, and the extremal-kernel bound of Chirre–Helfgott, preprint); the general unconditional scheme with a zero density as the general input and its density-free cases, and its published instances (Rosser–Schoenfeld, Schoenfeld, Dusart, Faber–Kadiri, Trudgian, Platt–Trudgian, Broadbent–Kadiri–Lumley–Ng–Wilk, Johnston–Yang, Fiori–Kadiri–Swidinsky, Axler; Fiori–Jaskari, preprint); explicit Mertens and prime-power sums (Ramaré corrected, Vanlalngaia, Axler, Lee–Nosal under RH; Broadbent–Fiori–Kadiri–Ng–Wilk, preprint); the n-th prime (Dusart, Axler); primes in progressions (Ramaré–Rumely, Dusart, McCurley, Bennett–Martin–O'Bryant–Rechnitzer, Ramaré, Lamzouri–Li–Soundararajan, Bach–Sorenson, Kadiri) and what a numerical real-zero gap removes from the exceptional clauses; short intervals (Schoenfeld, Ramaré–Saouter, Kadiri–Lumley, Cully-Hugill–Lee, Trudgian, Axler, Dusart, Dudek, Cully-Hugill, Cully-Hugill–Johnston).
